newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil opts to stay in Venezuela project.
newsitem.headline: Statoil opts to stay in Venezuela project.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it had decided to participate in continued planning of a production and upgrading project for heavy crude in Venezuela.

Around 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) of heavy crude from the Zuata area of the Orinoco Belt, about 200 kilometres southest of Caracas, will be piped to a new upgrading facility on the coast, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The plant will produce 175,000 bpd of high-value, light, sweet oil for export to international refineries. It is due to come on stream in 2002.

Total investment, including horizontal production wells, pipeline and upgrading plant, was put at 18 billion crowns. Statoil said that it would contribute 2.7 billion crowns to the project in line with its 15 percent interest.
Other participants are Total, Venezuela's Maraven and Norsk Hydro.
